title: Is Post-Construction Office Cleanup (Rough & Final) Included in Standard Cleaning or Billed Extra?
seoTitle: Is Post-Construction Office Cleanup Included or Billed Extra?
metaDescription: Learn why post-construction rough and final office cleanup is excluded from base janitorial contracts ($0.05–$0.20/sq ft) and how to audit work-order bids.
excerpt: Standard commercial janitorial contracts explicitly exclude construction debris, drywall dust extraction, and silicone/paint scraping from nightly retainers. Use this contract audit guide to tell when minor remodeling falls under base housekeeping versus when an extra work order is justified.
quickAnswer: Post-construction rough and final office cleanup is almost never included in a standard recurring janitorial contract ($0.05 to $0.20 per sq ft per visit) and is universally billed as a separate extra-charge project work order ($0.30 to $0.85 per sq ft combined across rough, final, and puff phases, or $55 to $95 per specialty labor hour). The only exception occurs when an office undergoes minor single-room maintenance (such as hanging a whiteboard or swapping 2–3 ceiling tiles) where cleanup takes under 15 minutes of standard nightly vacuuming, or when a vendor waives the final puff-clean fee as an onboarding incentive for signing a new 12-to-36-month janitorial agreement.

blocks.text: Why Standard Janitorial Contracts Explicitly Exclude Post-Construction Cleanup

Nearly every commercial janitorial Master Services Agreement (MSA) in the United States contains a Standard Exclusions clause tucked into Schedule A. Right alongside biohazard remediation, exterior high-rise rigging, and server-room subfloor cleaning sits a strict carve-out: 'Removal of construction debris, remodeling dust, paint overspray, drywall compound, or contractor waste is excluded from base nightly service and requires a separate signed work order.'

Facility managers occasionally push back on this extra charge for post-construction rough and final clean work orders—especially when they remodel a 1,500-square-foot conference room or breakroom while continuing to pay their full monthly janitorial retainer. However, the economics and equipment physics explain why a nightly crew cannot absorb construction turnover inside a $0.05 to $0.20 per-square-foot routine visit. Standard janitorial pricing assumes an ISSA production benchmark of 3,500 square feet per hour at $35 to $65 per labor hour. Post-construction cleanup requires top-to-bottom vertical and overhead detailing at 300 to 600 square feet per hour ($55 to $95 per specialty hour)—consuming six to ten times the labor per square foot while rapidly destroying standard vacuum filters with alkaline gypsum silica.

blocks.text: 5 Tasks That Trigger a Separate Post-Construction Work Order

When auditing a janitorial contractor's extra-service quote after an office renovation, look at the specific physical tasks required. If your general contractor (GC) left the suite in 'broom-swept' condition, any of the following five tasks legally and operationally cross the line from standard housekeeping into billable post-construction detailing:

items: 1. Manufacturer Sticker, Silicone Glaze, and Paint Overspray Scraping: Routine interior glass add-ons ($15 to $35 per visit) cover fingerprint wiping on glass doors. Removing factory barcodes, protective plastic film adhesive, and drywall primer specks from 40 glass partition panels requires wet razor-blading and brass squeegee passes.

2. Interior Millwork and Drawer Sawdust Extraction: Standard breakroom sanitation ($12 to $25 per visit) wipes exterior cabinet faces and countertops. Post-construction detailing requires vacuuming and damp-wiping the inside of every freshly hung cabinet box, drawer track, and hinge pocket.

3. Grout Haze & Porcelain Mortar Descaling: New restroom ceramic tile (1.12x base multiplier) and porcelain sinks arrive coated in polymeric grout haze and plumber's putty that ruin standard mop heads and demand non-rusting synthetic scouring agitation.

4. High-Reach Ceiling Grid, Troffer, and HVAC Diffuser Vacuuming: Nightly crews clean surfaces up to 7 feet. Post-construction crews must work off step ladders to vacuum settled gypsum powder off upper door frames, exposed spiral ductwork, and LED light lenses.

5. Fine Gypsum Silica Multi-Pass Floor Neutralization: Because drywall dust turns into chalky white streaks when wet-mopped with standard water, crews must perform multiple HEPA dry-vacuum and acidic/neutralizer rinse passes.

blocks.title: Check Whether Your General Contractor Already Charged You for Final Cleaning
blocks.text: Before paying your janitorial vendor an extra $0.35 to $0.65/sq ft for post-construction cleaning, audit your General Contractor's Schedule of Values under CSI Division 01 (General Requirements – Final Cleaning). Tenants frequently discover they already paid the GC $2,500 to $8,000 for a 'Final Clean,' yet the GC's labor sub only performed a 2-hour Phase 1 rough sweep. Hold the GC accountable or back-charge their retainage to fund your janitorial vendor's Phase 2/Phase 3 detail work order.
Commercial Detailing Tools That Separate Turnover Crews from Nightly Cleaners

Another way to verify whether a vendor is delivering genuine post-construction detailing—rather than charging specialty rates ($55 to $95/hr) while sending a basic nightly trash-and-dash crew—is inspecting the tools staged on site. Standard soft feather dusters and worn cotton string mops simply smear construction adhesive and gypsum grit across new finishes.

On a legitimate Phase 2 and Phase 3 turnover, technicians target fine perimeter grit using the O-Cedar Commercial MaxiClean Angle Broom & Lobby Pan (12-inch angled head with flagged polypropylene bristles on a 48-inch handle designed specifically to pull fine drywall and sawdust out of tight baseboard seams and elevator sill tracks without scattering dust airborne). In newly tiled restrooms and breakroom kitchenettes, crews remove hardened caulk, thin-set residue, and metal oxidation from stainless sinks and porcelain fixtures using 3M Scotch-Brite Commercial Heavy-Duty Scour Pads (20-Pack, 6x9-inch non-rusting synthetic scouring pads that leave zero metallic rust specks behind). Finally, for full-height conference room glass storefronts and lobby sidelights, technicians pair razor scrapers with the Ettore Master Brass 14-Inch Commercial Window Squeegee (solid tempered brass 14-inch channel and handle with replaceable professional streak-free rubber blade) to cut through silicone glazing film in a single sharp draw.
How to Negotiate Post-Construction Add-Ons Without Getting Overcharged
If your office is planning a remodeling project or moving into a newly built suite, follow this four-step contract strategy to minimize extra-charge invoices:

items.name: Step 1: Define a 15-Minute 'De Minimis' Maintenance Rule in Your Base Contract
items.text: Add a sentence to your janitorial agreement stating that localized dust cleanup from minor handyman repairs requiring under 15 minutes of sweeping and HEPA vacuuming on a scheduled service night is included at no extra charge.

items.name: Step 2: Use a New Annual Retainer to Negotiate a Free or 50%-Off Puff Clean
items.text: When moving into a new 10,000+ sq ft office where the GC completes the Phase 1 and Phase 2 clean, ask bidding janitorial firms to fold the Phase 3 pre-move-in Puff Clean ($0.08–$0.18/sq ft value) into the contract as a sign-on concession.

items.name: Step 3: Waive Standalone Trip Minimums by Scheduling Tag-On Shifts
items.text: For single-room renovations (under 1,500 sq ft), schedule your incumbent nightly crew to stay two extra hours after their normal shift at $55–$75/hr rather than paying an outside specialty vendor's $450–$750 standalone mobilization minimum.

items.name: Step 4: Require Pre- and Post-Clean Photo Documentation of Millwork & Glass
items.text: Before approving an extra work order invoice, verify that cabinet interiors, baseboard corners, restroom porcelain, and glass partitions pass a white-cloth swipe test.

faqs.q: Can our janitorial vendor void their contract or charge a damage fee if we make them vacuum drywall dust with their regular vacuums?
faqs.a: Yes. Fine gypsum drywall dust (2 to 10 microns) rapidly blinds standard commercial vacuum bags, overheats armature motors, and blows straight through non-HEPA exhaust ports across the rest of the office. Contractors explicitly exclude construction dust from base contracts to protect their on-site equipment and prevent cross-contaminating clean suites.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a GC's 'broom-clean' turnover and a janitorial 'white-glove final clean'?
faqs.a: A general contractor's 'broom-clean' turnover typically corresponds to a Phase 1 Rough Clean ($0.12–$0.25/sq ft): bulk scrap removed, floors swept, and visible stickers pulled off windows. It rarely includes damp microfiber wiping of settled airborne gypsum dust inside drawers, on top of door frames, or across glass partitions—which requires a Phase 2/Phase 3 janitorial detail clean ($0.25–$0.60/sq ft).

faqs.q: How should we price a small 500 sq ft conference room remodel with our existing nightly cleaner?
faqs.a: Because your incumbent janitorial crew is already on-site for your scheduled weekly or 5x/week service (eliminating drive time and the $350–$750 standalone project minimum), negotiate an hourly tag-on work order of 2 to 3 specialty labor hours at $55 to $85 per hour ($110 to $255 total) to cover HEPA vacuuming, baseboard sweeping, and glass squeegee detailing.

faqs.q: Do vendors charge extra for consumables and trash liners during a post-construction clean?
faqs.a: In standard ongoing agreements, paper, soap, and liner consumables add $0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit when vendor-supplied. During a post-construction final clean, heavy contractor drum liners, razor blades, scouring pads, and neutralizers are baked into the $0.30–$0.85/sq ft turnkey rate, though initial filling of restroom paper and soap dispensers prior to employee move-in is billed at your ongoing consumables rate or supplied by the tenant.
